goal: Fix a reload that overdraws the reserve and cap the reserve
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: when a player's reserve is low, reload takes more paintballs than they have and the reserve goes negative. Fix reload so it only moves what the reserve has, and make addReserve cap the reserve at a new constant MAX_RESERVE = 120. Keep everything else the same.

```lua
--!strict
-- AmmoService: magazine + reserve paintballs per player for the paintball markers.
local AmmoService = {}

export type AmmoState = {
	magazine: number,
	reserve: number,
	reloading: boolean,
}

local MAGAZINE_SIZE = 20
local START_RESERVE = 60
local states: { [any]: AmmoState } = {}

local function newState(): AmmoState
	return { magazine = MAGAZINE_SIZE, reserve = START_RESERVE, reloading = false }
end

function AmmoService.get(player: any): AmmoState
	local state = states[player]
	if state == nil then
		state = newState()
		states[player] = state
	end
	return state
end

-- Fires one paintball. Returns true when a shot was fired.
function AmmoService.fire(player: any): boolean
	local state = AmmoService.get(player)
	if state.reloading or state.magazine <= 0 then
		return false
	end
	state.magazine -= 1
	return true
end

-- Refills the magazine from the reserve. Returns how many paintballs were moved.
function AmmoService.reload(player: any): number
	local state = AmmoService.get(player)
	if state.reloading then
		return 0
	end
	state.reloading = true
	local missing = MAGAZINE_SIZE - state.magazine
	state.magazine += missing
	state.reserve -= missing
	state.reloading = false
	return missing
end

function AmmoService.addReserve(player: any, amount: number)
	local state = AmmoService.get(player)
	state.reserve += amount
end

function AmmoService.reset(player: any)
	states[player] = newState()
end

function AmmoService.remove(player: any)
	states[player] = nil
end

return AmmoService
```

```lua
-- TeamScore: points per team for one paintball round, with a change callback for the HUD.
local TeamScore = {}
TeamScore.__index = TeamScore

function TeamScore.new(teamNames, winScore)
	local self = setmetatable({}, TeamScore)
	self.scores = {}
	self.winScore = winScore or 50
	self.winner = nil
	self.listeners = {}
	for _, name in ipairs(teamNames) do
		self.scores[name] = 0
	end
	return self
end

function TeamScore:onChanged(fn)
	table.insert(self.listeners, fn)
end

function TeamScore:_emit(team)
	for _, fn in ipairs(self.listeners) do
		fn(team, self.scores[team])
	end
end

function TeamScore:addPoints(team, amount)
	self.scores[team] = self.scores[team] + amount
	if self.scores[team] >= self.winScore then
		self.winner = team
	end
	self:_emit(team)
end

function TeamScore:get(team)
	return self.scores[team]
end

function TeamScore:leader()
	local best, bestScore = nil, -1
	for team, score in pairs(self.scores) do
		if score > bestScore then
			best, bestScore = team, score
		end
	end
	return best
end

function TeamScore:standings()
	local list = {}
	for team, score in pairs(self.scores) do
		table.insert(list, { team = team, score = score })
	end
	table.sort(list, function(a, b)
		if a.score == b.score then
			return a.team < b.team
		end
		return a.score > b.score
	end)
```

goal: Fix a round timer that runs past zero and formats seconds wrong
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: this round timer keeps counting below zero and calls the finished handlers on every step after the end, and format() shows 1:5 instead of 1:05. Fix both: the time stops at 0, the timer stops running, onFinished handlers run exactly once, onSecond never reports a negative number, and format() is m:ss.

```lua
-- RoundTimer: counts a paintball round down. The server calls step(dt) from RunService.Heartbeat.
local RoundTimer = {}
RoundTimer.__index = RoundTimer

function RoundTimer.new(duration)
	return setmetatable({
		duration = duration,
		remaining = duration,
		running = false,
		finishedHandlers = {},
		secondHandlers = {},
		lastWhole = math.ceil(duration),
	}, RoundTimer)
end

function RoundTimer:start()
	self.running = true
end

function RoundTimer:pause()
	self.running = false
end

function RoundTimer:isRunning()
	return self.running
end

function RoundTimer:onFinished(fn)
	table.insert(self.finishedHandlers, fn)
end

function RoundTimer:onSecond(fn)
	table.insert(self.secondHandlers, fn)
end

function RoundTimer:addTime(seconds)
	self.remaining += seconds
end

function RoundTimer:reset()
	self.remaining = self.duration
	self.lastWhole = math.ceil(self.duration)
	self.running = false
end

function RoundTimer:step(dt)
	if not self.running then
		return
	end
	self.remaining -= dt
	local whole = math.ceil(self.remaining)
	if whole ~= self.lastWhole then
		self.lastWhole = whole
		for _, fn in ipairs(self.secondHandlers) do
			fn(whole)
		end
	end
	if self.remaining <= 0 then
		for _, fn in ipairs(self.finishedHandlers) do
			fn()
		end
	end
end

function RoundTimer:format()
	local seconds = math.ceil(self.remaining)
	return string.format("%d:%d", seconds // 60, seconds % 60)
end

return RoundTimer
```

goal: Stop double releases in an object pool and cap its free list
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: my splat decal pool breaks when the same splat is released twice: it goes into the free list twice and two hits end up sharing one decal. Make release ignore splats that are not active, and never keep more than maxSize splats in the free list: extra released splats go to an optional destroy callback, a new third parameter of SplatPool.new.

```lua
-- SplatPool: reuses paint splat decals instead of creating a new one for every hit.
local SplatPool = {}
SplatPool.__index = SplatPool

function SplatPool.new(create, maxSize)
	local self = setmetatable({}, SplatPool)
	self.create = create
	self.maxSize = maxSize or 50
	self.free = {}
	self.active = {}
	self.created = 0
	return self
end

function SplatPool:acquire()
	local splat = table.remove(self.free)
	if splat == nil then
		splat = self.create()
		self.created += 1
	end
	self.active[splat] = true
	return splat
end

function SplatPool:release(splat)
	self.active[splat] = nil
	table.insert(self.free, splat)
end

function SplatPool:activeCount()
	local n = 0
	for _ in pairs(self.active) do
		n += 1
	end
	return n
end

function SplatPool:freeCount()
	return #self.free
end

function SplatPool:releaseAll()
	local list = {}
	for splat in pairs(self.active) do
		table.insert(list, splat)
	end
	for _, splat in ipairs(list) do
		self:release(splat)
	end
end

function SplatPool:prewarm(count)
	for _ = 1, count do
		local splat = self.create()
		self.created += 1
		table.insert(self.free, splat)
	end
end

return SplatPool
```

goal: Make ability cooldowns per player and tolerate unknown abilities
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: when one player uses dash, every other player's dash goes on cooldown too. Fix it so cooldowns are per player. Unknown ability names must make ready and use return false instead of erroring, and clear(player) must forget only that player's cooldowns.

```lua
-- Cooldowns: ability cooldowns for the paintball abilities (dash, shield, grenade). Server only.
local Cooldowns = {}

local DURATIONS = {
	dash = 3,
	shield = 12,
	grenade = 8,
}

local lastUsed = {}

-- Replaced in tests; os.clock on the server.
Cooldowns.clock = os.clock

function Cooldowns.duration(ability)
	return DURATIONS[ability]
end

function Cooldowns.ready(player, ability)
	local last = lastUsed[ability]
	if last == nil then
		return true
	end
	return Cooldowns.clock() - last >= DURATIONS[ability]
end

function Cooldowns.use(player, ability)
	if not Cooldowns.ready(player, ability) then
		return false
	end
	lastUsed[ability] = Cooldowns.clock()
	return true
end

function Cooldowns.remaining(player, ability)
	local last = lastUsed[ability]
	if last == nil then
		return 0
	end
	return math.max(0, DURATIONS[ability] - (Cooldowns.clock() - last))
end

function Cooldowns.clear(player)
	lastUsed = {}
end

return Cooldowns
```

```lua
-- Inventory: paint grenades, health packs and power-ups a player carries between rounds.
local Inventory = {}
Inventory.__index = Inventory

local MAX_STACK = 99

function Inventory.new(owner)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Inventory)
	self.owner = owner
	self.items = {}
	self.changed = {}
	return self
end

function Inventory:OnChanged(fn)
	table.insert(self.changed, fn)
end

function Inventory:_notify(item)
	for _, fn in ipairs(self.changed) do
		fn(item, self:GetCount(item))
	end
end

function Inventory:GetCount(item)
	return self.items[item] or 0
end

function Inventory:HasItem(item, amount)
	return self:GetCount(item) >= (amount or 1)
end

function Inventory:AddItem(item, amount)
	local total = math.min(MAX_STACK, self:GetCount(item) + amount)
	self.items[item] = total
	self:_notify(item)
	return total
end

function Inventory:RemoveItem(item, amount)
	local left = self:GetCount(item) - amount
	if left <= 0 then
		self.items[item] = nil
	else
		self.items[item] = left
	end
	self:_notify(item)
	return true
end

function Inventory:Snapshot()
	local copy = {}
	for item in pairs(self.items) do
		copy[item] = self:GetCount(item)
	end
	return copy
end

function Inventory:Clear()
	for item in pairs(self.items) do
		self.items[item] = nil
		self:_notify(item)
	end
```

goal: Add headshots to a damage calculator and clamp armor
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: add headshots to this damage module. compute gets a 4th parameter headshot (boolean). A headshot multiplies the damage by HEADSHOT_MULTIPLIER = 2 before armor is applied, except the shotgun, which uses 1.25. Also clamp armor to 0..0.8 so armor can never block everything.

```lua
-- Damage: hit damage for the paintball markers, with distance falloff and armor.
local Damage = {}

Damage.BASE = {
	pistol = 20,
	rifle = 34,
	shotgun = 12,
	sniper = 80,
}
Damage.PELLETS = {
	shotgun = 8,
}
Damage.FALLOFF_START = 40
Damage.FALLOFF_END = 120
Damage.MIN_FACTOR = 0.4

-- 1 up to FALLOFF_START studs, then linear down to MIN_FACTOR at FALLOFF_END.
function Damage.falloff(distance)
	if distance <= Damage.FALLOFF_START then
		return 1
	end
	if distance >= Damage.FALLOFF_END then
		return Damage.MIN_FACTOR
	end
	local t = (distance - Damage.FALLOFF_START) / (Damage.FALLOFF_END - Damage.FALLOFF_START)
	return 1 - t * (1 - Damage.MIN_FACTOR)
end

function Damage.pellets(weapon)
	return Damage.PELLETS[weapon] or 1
end

-- Damage of one hit (one pellet for the shotgun). armor is 0..1 (fraction blocked).
function Damage.compute(weapon, distance, armor)
	local base = Damage.BASE[weapon]
	if base == nil then
		error("unknown weapon " .. tostring(weapon))
	end
	local dmg = base * Damage.falloff(distance)
	dmg = dmg * (1 - (armor or 0))
	return math.floor(dmg + 0.5)
end

-- Total damage when every pellet hits.
function Damage.volley(weapon, distance, armor)
	return Damage.compute(weapon, distance, armor) * Damage.pellets(weapon)
end

return Damage
```

goal: Scale projectile gravity by dt and stop at max range
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: my paintballs fall too slowly when the frame rate is high, because gravity is added once per step instead of being scaled by dt. Fix step so the velocity changes by GRAVITY * dt and the position by velocity * dt, and make step return false (and stop moving the ball) once the ball has travelled more than MAX_RANGE studs in total.

```lua
-- Projectile: client-side paintball flight. Vectors are plain {x, y, z} tables so the server can share it.
local Projectile = {}
Projectile.__index = Projectile

Projectile.GRAVITY = -60
Projectile.MAX_RANGE = 300

local function length(v)
	return math.sqrt(v.x * v.x + v.y * v.y + v.z * v.z)
end

function Projectile.new(origin, velocity)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Projectile)
	self.position = { x = origin.x, y = origin.y, z = origin.z }
	self.velocity = { x = velocity.x, y = velocity.y, z = velocity.z }
	self.travelled = 0
	self.alive = true
	return self
end

-- Advances the ball by dt seconds. Returns true while the ball is still flying.
function Projectile:step(dt)
	if not self.alive then
		return false
	end
	self.velocity.y += Projectile.GRAVITY
	local move = {
		x = self.velocity.x * dt,
		y = self.velocity.y * dt,
		z = self.velocity.z * dt,
	}
	self.position.x += move.x
	self.position.y += move.y
	self.position.z += move.z
	self.travelled += length(move)
	return true
end

function Projectile:speed()
	return length(self.velocity)
end

function Projectile:kill()
	self.alive = false
end

-- Simulates until the ball dies or `seconds` pass; returns the positions for a debug beam.
function Projectile:trace(seconds, dt)
	local points = {}
	local t = 0
	while t < seconds and self:step(dt) do
		table.insert(points, { x = self.position.x, y = self.position.y, z = self.position.z })
		t += dt
	end
	return points
end

return Projectile
```

goal: Fix an off-by-one rate limiter and stop blocked calls counting
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: my RemoteEvent rate limiter lets 11 calls through per window when the limit is 10. Fix that, make blocked calls not count toward the window, and add a forget(player) method that I can call from Players.PlayerRemoving.

```lua
-- RateLimiter: per-player limit for RemoteEvent calls (fire, reload, chat ping). Server only.
local RateLimiter = {}
RateLimiter.__index = RateLimiter

function RateLimiter.new(limit, window, clock)
	local self = setmetatable({}, RateLimiter)
	self.limit = limit
	self.window = window
	self.clock = clock or os.clock
	self.records = {}
	self.blocked = 0
	return self
end

-- Returns true when this call is allowed.
function RateLimiter:allow(player)
	local now = self.clock()
	local record = self.records[player]
	if record == nil or now - record.start >= self.window then
		record = { start = now, count = 0 }
		self.records[player] = record
	end
	record.count += 1
	if record.count <= self.limit + 1 then
		return true
	end
	self.blocked += 1
	return false
end

function RateLimiter:remaining(player)
	local record = self.records[player]
	if record == nil or self.clock() - record.start >= self.window then
		return self.limit
	end
	return math.max(0, self.limit - record.count)
end

function RateLimiter:wrap(handler)
	return function(player, ...)
		if not self:allow(player) then
			return
		end
		return handler(player, ...)
	end
end

function RateLimiter:stats()
	local players = 0
	for _ in pairs(self.records) do
		players += 1
	end
	return { players = players, blocked = self.blocked }
end

return RateLimiter
```

goal: Break team-size ties by score and add rebalance
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: when both teams have the same number of players, assign() should put the new player on the team with the lower score (it always picks the last team now). Also add rebalance(teams) that moves players from the biggest team to the smallest until the sizes differ by at most 1, moving the most recently joined players first; it returns the list of moved players.

```lua
-- TeamBalancer: picks a team for players who join mid-match.
-- teams = { { name = "Red", players = { ... }, score = 0 }, ... }; players are in join order.
local TeamBalancer = {}

local function sizeOf(team)
	return #team.players
end

function TeamBalancer.smallest(teams)
	local target = teams[1]
	for _, team in ipairs(teams) do
		if sizeOf(team) <= sizeOf(target) then
			target = team
		end
	end
	return target
end

function TeamBalancer.assign(teams, player)
	local team = TeamBalancer.smallest(teams)
	table.insert(team.players, player)
	return team
end

function TeamBalancer.remove(teams, player)
	for _, team in ipairs(teams) do
		local index = table.find(team.players, player)
		if index then
			table.remove(team.players, index)
			return team
		end
	end
	return nil
end

function TeamBalancer.teamOf(teams, player)
	for _, team in ipairs(teams) do
		if table.find(team.players, player) then
			return team
		end
	end
	return nil
end

function TeamBalancer.sizes(teams)
	local out = {}
	for _, team in ipairs(teams) do
		out[team.name] = sizeOf(team)
	end
	return out
end

return TeamBalancer
```

goal: Add a validated sensitivity setting and clamp fov
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: add a new setting sensitivity to this settings validator: a number, default 1, allowed 0.1 to 5; values outside the range are clamped and non-numbers become the default. Also fix fov: values outside 60..110 must be clamped to the range, not reset to the default.

```lua
-- SettingsValidator: cleans the settings table a client sends with RemoteFunction SaveSettings.
-- Never trust the client: unknown keys are dropped and every value is checked.
local SettingsValidator = {}

local DEFAULTS = {
	fov = 70,
	volume = 0.8,
	invertY = false,
	crosshair = "dot",
}

local CROSSHAIRS = {
	dot = true,
	cross = true,
	circle = true,
}

local function number(value, default)
	if type(value) ~= "number" or value ~= value then
		return default
	end
	return value
end

function SettingsValidator.defaults()
	return table.clone(DEFAULTS)
end

function SettingsValidator.clean(raw)
	local out = SettingsValidator.defaults()
	if type(raw) ~= "table" then
		return out
	end
	local fov = number(raw.fov, DEFAULTS.fov)
	if fov < 60 or fov > 110 then
		fov = DEFAULTS.fov
	end
	out.fov = fov
	out.volume = math.clamp(number(raw.volume, DEFAULTS.volume), 0, 1)
	if type(raw.invertY) == "boolean" then
		out.invertY = raw.invertY
	end
	if type(raw.crosshair) == "string" and CROSSHAIRS[raw.crosshair] then
		out.crosshair = raw.crosshair
	end
	return out
end

function SettingsValidator.changed(old, new)
	local keys = {}
	for key, value in pairs(new) do
		if old[key] ~= value then
			table.insert(keys, key)
		end
	end
	table.sort(keys)
	return keys
end

return SettingsValidator
```

goal: Reset streaks on death, track the best streak, reward exact milestones
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: fix this kill streak tracker. A death must reset that player's streak to 0. Add bestOf(player) that returns the best streak the player ever had (it survives deaths). Rewards must only be given when the streak reaches exactly 3, 5 or 10, not on every kill after 3.

```lua
-- Streaks: kill streak rewards for paintball (3 = radar ping, 5 = paint grenade, 10 = airstrike).
local Streaks = {}
Streaks.__index = Streaks

local REWARDS = {
	[3] = "RadarPing",
	[5] = "PaintGrenade",
	[10] = "Airstrike",
}

function Streaks.new()
	local self = setmetatable({}, Streaks)
	self.current = {}
	self.given = {}
	return self
end

function Streaks:streakOf(player)
	return self.current[player] or 0
end

-- The reward the streak earns at this kill count, or nil.
function Streaks:rewardFor(streak)
	local best = nil
	for count, reward in pairs(REWARDS) do
		if streak >= count and (best == nil or count > best.count) then
			best = { count = count, reward = reward }
		end
	end
	return best and best.reward
end

-- Call when `player` gets a kill. Returns the reward to give now, or nil.
function Streaks:kill(player)
	local streak = self:streakOf(player) + 1
	self.current[player] = streak
	local reward = self:rewardFor(streak)
	if reward then
		self.given[player] = (self.given[player] or 0) + 1
	end
	return reward
end

function Streaks:death(player)
	self.given[player] = 0
end

function Streaks:rewardsGiven(player)
	return self.given[player] or 0
end

function Streaks:remove(player)
	self.current[player] = nil
	self.given[player] = nil
end

return Streaks
```

goal: Pick the safest spawn instead of the most dangerous one
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: pick() returns the spawn that is closest to the enemies. It must return the spawn whose nearest enemy is farthest away. Also skip spawns marked blocked = true, and with no enemies return the first spawn that is not blocked.

```lua
-- SpawnPicker: chooses where a respawning paintball player appears.
-- Positions are {x, y, z} tables; spawns = { { name = "A", position = {...}, blocked = false }, ... }
local SpawnPicker = {}

local function distance(a, b)
	local dx, dy, dz = a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y, a.z - b.z
	return math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
end

-- Distance from `position` to the closest enemy (math.huge without enemies).
function SpawnPicker.nearestEnemy(position, enemies)
	local best = math.huge
	for _, enemy in ipairs(enemies) do
		local d = distance(position, enemy)
		if d < best then
			best = d
		end
	end
	return best
end

function SpawnPicker.pick(spawns, enemies)
	local best, bestDistance = nil, math.huge
	for _, spawn in ipairs(spawns) do
		local d = SpawnPicker.nearestEnemy(spawn.position, enemies)
		if d < bestDistance then
			best, bestDistance = spawn, d
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- Spawns sorted from safest to most dangerous, for the debug overlay.
function SpawnPicker.ranked(spawns, enemies)
	local list = table.clone(spawns)
	table.sort(list, function(a, b)
		return SpawnPicker.nearestEnemy(a.position, enemies) > SpawnPicker.nearestEnemy(b.position, enemies)
	end)
	return list
end

function SpawnPicker.distance(a, b)
	return distance(a, b)
end

return SpawnPicker
```

goal: Fix clock formatting: padding, hours and negative input
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: clock(seconds) prints 1:5 instead of 1:05. Fix it, show h:mm:ss when the time is an hour or more, and treat negative input as 0 (0:00). words() has the same negative problem: it should say 0 s.

```lua
-- TimeFormat: text for the round timer, the lobby countdown and the match history screen.
local TimeFormat = {}

-- 65 -> "1:05"
function TimeFormat.clock(seconds)
	local whole = math.floor(seconds)
	local minutes = whole // 60
	local rest = whole % 60
	return minutes .. ":" .. rest
end

-- 125 -> "2 min 5 s"
function TimeFormat.words(seconds)
	local whole = math.floor(seconds)
	local minutes = whole // 60
	local rest = whole % 60
	if minutes == 0 then
		return rest .. " s"
	end
	if rest == 0 then
		return minutes .. " min"
	end
	return minutes .. " min " .. rest .. " s"
end

-- "1:05" -> 65; nil for text that is not a clock.
function TimeFormat.parse(text)
	local m, s = string.match(text, "^(%d+):(%d%d)$")
	if m == nil then
		return nil
	end
	return tonumber(m) * 60 + tonumber(s)
end

-- Countdown text with tenths in the last ten seconds: "9.4".
function TimeFormat.countdown(seconds)
	if seconds < 10 then
		return string.format("%.1f", math.max(0, seconds))
	end
	return TimeFormat.clock(seconds)
end

function TimeFormat.ago(seconds)
	if seconds < 60 then
		return "just now"
	end
	return TimeFormat.words(seconds) .. " ago"
end

return TimeFormat
```

goal: Add once() to an event bus and fix skipped handlers
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: add once(name, fn) to this event bus: the handler runs for the next emit of that event only. Also, when a handler disconnects itself during emit, the handler after it is skipped; fix that so every handler that was connected when emit started still runs once.

```lua
-- EventBus: in-game events (RoundStarted, PlayerSplatted, FlagCaptured) shared by server modules.
local EventBus = {}
EventBus.__index = EventBus

function EventBus.new()
	local self = setmetatable({}, EventBus)
	self.handlers = {}
	self.counts = {}
	return self
end

function EventBus:on(name, fn)
	local list = self.handlers[name]
	if list == nil then
		list = {}
		self.handlers[name] = list
	end
	table.insert(list, fn)
	local connection = {}
	function connection.disconnect()
		local index = table.find(list, fn)
		if index then
			table.remove(list, index)
		end
	end
	return connection
end

function EventBus:emit(name, ...)
	self.counts[name] = (self.counts[name] or 0) + 1
	local list = self.handlers[name]
	if list == nil then
		return 0
	end
	local ran = 0
	local i = 1
	while i <= #list do
		list[i](...)
		ran += 1
		i += 1
	end
	return ran
end

function EventBus:count(name)
	return self.counts[name] or 0
end

function EventBus:listeners(name)
	local list = self.handlers[name]
	return list and #list or 0
end

function EventBus:clear(name)
	self.handlers[name] = nil
end

return EventBus
```

goal: Count stack weight and refuse overweight adds
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball game: totalWeight() ignores how many of each item the backpack holds. Fix it, and make add() refuse (return false and change nothing) when the new total weight would go over self.maxWeight. Unknown items weigh 1.

```lua
-- Backpack: what a player carries into a paintball round. Weight limits how much gear they can take.
local Backpack = {}
Backpack.__index = Backpack

local WEIGHTS = {
	paintball_pod = 0.5,
	grenade = 2,
	medkit = 3,
	shield = 6,
}

function Backpack.new(maxWeight)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Backpack)
	self.maxWeight = maxWeight or 20
	self.items = {}
	return self
end

function Backpack.weightOf(item)
	return WEIGHTS[item]
end

function Backpack:count(item)
	return self.items[item] or 0
end

function Backpack:totalWeight()
	local total = 0
	for item in pairs(self.items) do
		total += Backpack.weightOf(item)
	end
	return total
end

function Backpack:add(item, count)
	count = count or 1
	self.items[item] = self:count(item) + count
	return true
end

function Backpack:remove(item, count)
	count = count or 1
	if self:count(item) < count then
		return false
	end
	local left = self:count(item) - count
	self.items[item] = if left > 0 then left else nil
	return true
end

function Backpack:freeWeight()
	return self.maxWeight - self:totalWeight()
end

function Backpack:list()
	local out = {}
	for item, count in pairs(self.items) do
		table.insert(out, { item = item, count = count })
	end
	table.sort(out, function(a, b)
		return a.item < b.item
	end)
	return out
end

return Backpack
```

goal: Return dropped flags home and handle teammates touching them
prompt:
In my Roblox paintball capture-the-flag mode: a dropped flag never returns home. Fix drop/update so a flag that stays dropped for returnTime seconds goes home (state 'home', no carrier). Also only the enemy team may pick a flag up; a teammate touching their own dropped flag returns it home at once (touch should return 'returned' in that case).

```lua
-- Flag: one team's flag in capture the flag. States: "home", "carried", "dropped".
local Flag = {}
Flag.__index = Flag

function Flag.new(team, returnTime)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Flag)
	self.team = team
	self.returnTime = returnTime or 30
	self.state = "home"
	self.carrier = nil
	self.droppedAt = nil
	self.dropPosition = nil
	return self
end

-- A player of `playerTeam` touches the flag at time `now`. Returns what happened, or nil.
function Flag:touch(player, playerTeam, now)
	if self.state == "carried" then
		return nil
	end
	self.state = "carried"
	self.carrier = player
	return "taken"
end

-- The carrier was splatted at `position`.
function Flag:drop(position, now)
	if self.state ~= "carried" then
		return
	end
	self.state = "dropped"
	self.carrier = nil
	self.dropPosition = position
end

-- Called every second by the round script.
function Flag:update(now)
	if self.state == "dropped" and self.droppedAt and now - self.droppedAt >= self.returnTime then
		self:returnHome()
	end
end

function Flag:returnHome()
	self.state = "home"
	self.carrier = nil
	self.droppedAt = nil
	self.dropPosition = nil
end

-- The carrier reached their own base.
function Flag:capture()
	if self.state ~= "carried" then
		return false
	end
	self:returnHome()
	return true
end

function Flag:isHome()
	return self.state == "home"
end

return Flag
```
